why: Resolving f first, a's ${?f} closes the cycle and is missing, so a is {t: 1} and f is a.t then x, "1x". Resolving a first, f's ${?a.t} closes it, f is "x", and a is the object {t: 1} followed by the text "x", an error (L373-374, L384-385). The order is undefined, so either result or an error is allowed (L866-881). typesafe/config 1.4.9 gives f = "x", a = {t: 1}: it takes a first, then silently drops the text next to the object — the same leniency as string-value-concatenation/010 and 015; lightbend/config#862 (on main) makes that a WrongType, which is the rejected outcome already in also_valid. In 044, the same cycle without the x, it gives f = 1
